title: Descent with divergence and extinction produces groups subordinate to groups

fields.label: Label
fields.value: Descent with divergence and extinction produces groups subordinate to groups

fields.label: Statement
fields.value: The nested arrangement of organisms into groups within groups (species within genera, genera within families, and so on) results from the modified descendants of a single progenitor diverging in character while less divergent forms are exterminated.

fields.label: Work
fields.value: On the Origin of Species by Means of Natural Selection, or the Preservation of Favoured Races in the Struggle for Life

fields.label: Chapter
fields.value: Ch. XIII: Mutual Affinities of Organic Beings: Morphology: Embryology: Rudimentary Organs

fields.label: Quotation
fields.value: he will see that the inevitable result is that the modified descendants proceeding from one progenitor become broken up into groups subordinate to groups.

fields.label: Agent
fields.value: delphisci Origin of Species claim extractor

fields.label: Assumptions
fields.value: Charles Darwin, On the Origin of Species (1st ed., London: John Murray, 1859), Chapter XIII, “Mutual Affinities of Organic Beings: Morphology: Embryology: Rudimentary Organs”; section “CLASSIFICATION, groups subordinate to groups”. Scope: all organic beings, living and extinct

fields.label: Assessment
fields.value: GPT-5.6 Sol on darwin1859-ch13-01: partially-resolvable, resolvability 0.72

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: Nested descent is exceptionally well documented, but attributing the hierarchy specifically to divergence plus extermination is model-dependent. Phylogenies used to test the claim can introduce circularity unless built from independent characters.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Quantify hierarchical phylogenetic structure and compare diversification models with descent, trait divergence and extinction against models lacking those processes. Support requires nested monophyletic clusters and model evidence that divergence plus lineage loss generated observed gaps.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Nestedness partly follows from tree-based representation.

Extinction histories are incomplete and alternative diversification processes can yield similar patterns.

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: Nested taxonomy is visible in existing trees, but the claim is a mechanism, and several branching models produce the same nesting. Sequence archives and the fossil record can test tree-likeness and the presence of extinct intermediates, which is only part of the causal story. A careful model comparison is feasible for major clades and does not cleanly separate this mechanism from simpler alternatives.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Ask whether character data from living and fossil organisms fit a branching hierarchy better than non-hierarchical or highly reticulate alternatives, and whether extinction of intermediate branches is required to reproduce the observed gaps between named groups. The claim is confirmed if tree-like structure is strong and simulated divergence without extinction of intermediates fails to produce the observed rank gaps, and refuted if the data are poorly hierarchical or gaps arise without that extinction.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Building a tree and then reading nested groups off it is circular unless the test is a fit comparison against non-tree models.

Horizontal transfer, hybridization and uneven fossil recovery all reduce the clarity of the hierarchy.

A pure branching process produces nested groups even when extinction is random, so the specific role of exterminating less divergent forms is hard to isolate.

data adequacy: 0.65
discriminating power: 0.45
